name: law_firm_software_020_grant_coauthor_workload_report
instruction: Build the firm's grant-writing workload report for this episode, batched under the episode batch code (ops_meta, meta_key='episode_state'; the episode row also carries the episode date and the workload_share_cutoff knob that decides who gets a capacity alert). The firm's fee-earner roster lives in the staff_roster collection — read it live and apply its active-at-episode-date rule; do not rely on any prose roster or on the names that happen to appear in the application data. For every active roster employee, push one ops_reports row (report='grant_workload', batch_code) carrying their grant involvements in each role (an application counts once per role a person holds on it — leading a application and co-authoring it are two involvements), their total logged hours, and their share of the firm's total grant involvements. STAGE 2 — firm policy SEVERITY-01 requires a report that summarizes another to reuse the summarized rows' values rather than recompute them: rank the workload rows by share and push one ops_reports row per rank (report='grant_workload_ranking', batch_code) carrying the rank, the employee's identity and their share. STAGE 3 — for every employee whose share exceeds the episode row's workload_share_cutoff, open a capacity-review task (tasks collection) assigned to the firm's supervising partner as identified from the roster. No other ops_reports rows for these reports and this batch, and no other tasks rows, may exist. Every collection this task doesn't write to must remain untouched.

hazards.mechanism: Departed-employee volume: EMP-006 (Dana Counsel) left the firm (staff_roster.active_to in the past) but still leads 3 grant applications (snapshot-confirmed: 3). A roster taken from prose or from the application data includes EMP-006 and produces 6 workload rows with wrong shares; the live roster has 5 active employees and EMP-006 must be absent from every report row.

The role double-count rule: application APP-2026-010 lists EMP-001 as lead author AND in its co_authors array, so that single application contributes two involvements (one per role) to EMP-001's counts and to the firm total (snapshot total: 599 involvements across the 5 active employees). Deduplicating roles per application yields a plausible total of 598 and shifts every share.

co_authors is a JSON array requiring membership testing, not equality: counting applications via equality (or counting an application once per employee while dropping the lead/co-author overlap) silently under-counts. The ranking's tie-break (equal shares ordered by employee id) is also enforced by the verifier.

success_criteria.summary: Exactly one grant_workload row per active roster employee (5 in the snapshot), every count dual-path (Python array-membership filtering and SQL lead GROUP BY / jsonb co-author membership), share math exact including the double-counted application, EMP-006 absent everywhere, ranking ties per policy, and capacity-alert tasks written to the roster-derived supervising partner for the above-cutoff slice.

checks.expect: one grant_workload row per active roster employee, one grant_workload_ranking row per employee, capacity-alert tasks for the above-cutoff slice
lead and co-author counts agree between Python array-membership filtering and SQL (GROUP BY lead_author; jsonb co-author membership)
including departed EMP-006, deduplicating an employee's lead+co-author roles on one application, or ranking by billable hours instead of share => FAIL

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: The only task in the suite combining a live-roster read (departed employee excluded, 3 near-miss applications led by them), array-membership counting with an explicit lead+co-author double-count case, a cross-collection hours figure, and capacity alerts that write back into tasks with a roster-derived assignee.
